title: Redwood POC weekly sync - Quantaco AI - cost/econ review
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on unit economics: tokens/sec/$, caching and batching tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: run 5k prompt benchmark on dedicated config, share updated cost model, and schedule a performance deep dive next Tuesday.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Mike Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Quantaco CTO), Lina Gomez (ML Eng), Tom Wu (Infra)

[00:00] Mike: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda — cost/unit econ review, tuning notes, and next steps. we only have 45 so we'll focus on the numbers from last week's run.
[00:18] Raj: yep sounds good, we've had some questions from the finance team about the tokens per dollar numbers.
[00:24] Priya: cool, i'll kick off with the high level bench marks we ran friday - note some of the timestamps in the logs are a bit off, system clock drift on the agent.
[00:34] Priya: baseline was hosted small instance, 8k sequence mix, mixed prompt lengths - average tokens/sec about 1,200, cost about $0.018 per 1k tokens which yields roughly tokens per dollar around 66k tokens per dollar on that config.
[00:52] Lina: i thought previous email said 80k tokens per dollar?
[00:58] Priya: yeah that was with prefix caching enabled and longer sequences, the baseline no-cache number was lower. with prefix/KV caching on we saw an effective tokens/sec jump to 1,850 and tokens per dollar up to ~102k. caveat: that's for our synthetic workload where 40% of tokens were repeat prefixes.
[01:20] Tom: quick q, when you say KV cache, is that session-level or prefix-only?
[01:25] Priya: it's prefix KV cache — we cache the model KV for frequent prefixes across requests. the log shows cache hit rate around 42% for the test run. note the transcript has some typos, KV cash at times in logs.
[01:40] Mike: important to call out tradeoffs — caching reduces cost but can increase tail latency for cold prefixes if eviction happens. also impacts memory footprint on dedicated nodes.
[01:53] Raj: what about batching effects? our main worry is latency SLOs for interactive features.
[01:59] Priya: good point — we ran a batching sweep. with a 20ms batch window we get 2,600 tokens/sec aggregate but p95 latency moves from 120ms to about 240ms. with 5ms window tokens/sec drops to 1,900 but p95 is under 150ms. so it's a latency vs cost dial.
[02:20] Lina: can you remind me the cost delta between hosted and dedicated for our committed profile?
[02:25] Mike: for your projected 1M tokens/day, hosted price with our model variant is ~ $180/month; dedicated reserved compute amortized is about $120/month if you commit to a small pool — those numbers assume no caching. with caching the dedicated case improves more because you get higher hit rates.
[02:42] Raj: those sound promising. is the dedicated number including autoscale bursts?
[02:47] Mike: reserved capacity pricing covers baseline; bursts are billed extra, we can show a cost band. Priya has the burst math.
[02:54] Priya: yes bursts are modeled — for cost-econ we used a 20% burst factor which added ~15% to monthly ops cost in the spreadsheet.
[03:03] Tom: any changes needed on our infra side to run the dedicated test?
[03:07] Priya: we need VPC peering and a couple of firewall rules, and we recommend enabling our latency optimized kernel for the instance. the dedicated test will also attempt prefix cache warmup so you might see short CPU spikes.
[03:23] Raj: okay can the test be run behind our IP allowlist?
[03:26] Mike: yes we support IP allowlist and private control plane—Priya will coordinate.
[03:31] Lina: curious about quantization impact — we tried int8 on a small model internally and saw some drop in quality.
[03:37] Priya: we did a quick quantization sweep — int8 gave ~1.6x tokens/sec improvement and a cost reduction of ~35% at the expense of minor n-gram quality diffs on the open eval set. for some prompt types quality delta is negligible but for many-shot few-shot it can matter. we recommend running your eval set.
[03:56] Raj: let's make sure we measure hallucination rate as well, finance will want assurance on quality.
[04:00] Mike: agreed — action: we'll run the 5k prompt set with ground truth labels and report precision/recall and hallucination metrics.
[04:07] Priya: also want to call out routing options — you can route low-latency traffic to a smaller, hotter pool and high-throughput to larger batch pools. that hybrid gives best cost/lats balance.
[04:18] Tom: that seems useful. does Redwood charge extra for routing policies?
[04:22] Mike: routing configuration is part of the Dedicated feature set; there's no per-policy fee, it's included. only capacity and burst usage billed.
[04:29] Raj: any competitor notes? we showed Anthropic last week as a benchmark to execs.
[04:33] Priya: yeah Anthropic numbers were close on latency but cost per token higher; OpenAI was cheaper on small short requests but their batching profile is different. internal infra would need more ops headcount.
[04:45] Lina: can you share the raw logs so our infra team can double-check the accounting?
[04:49] Mike: yes we'll provide logs, plus the cost spreadsheet.
[04:52] Priya: quick callout on cache warmup — the first 1-2 hours of a warmup run have lower hit rates; the steady state is what the spreadsheet uses. we should run the dedicated test for at least 4 hours to reach steady state.
[05:06] Raj: ok makes sense. timeline — finance wants a final cost estimate by next friday. is that doable?
[05:11] Mike: yes, if we run the 4-hour steady benchmark early next week and you provide prompt mix, we can deliver a finalized cost model by 2026-06-26.
[05:20] Lina: one more question — on log retention and audit, will we get token-level usage for billing reconciliation?
[05:26] Mike: yes we provide per-request token counts, and we can add token attribution by route. audit logs are available as an add-on with longer retention.
[05:33] Tom: from infra side i'll need the VPC peering steps doc.
[05:36] Priya: i'll share the VPC runbook and firewall rules in the follow up.
[05:40] Mike: great — let's go through the numbers quickly — (Mike shares screen) the sheet shows three scenarios: no-cache hosted, cache-enabled hosted, cache-enabled dedicated. tokens per dollar numbers 66k, 102k, 145k respectively for the sample traffic.
[05:58] Raj: 145k tokens/dollar on dedicated with caching is very compelling. is that with quantization?
[06:02] Priya: that's without quantization. if you add int8 quant we get to ~230k tokens/dollar but again quality caveats.
[06:12] Lina: can we try an experiment where we quantize only the background rerank model and keep generation at fp16?
[06:18] Priya: yes hybrid quantization is supported and often yields good cost benefits while preserving generation quality. we'll include a hybrid run in the tests.
[06:27] Mike: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners.
[06:31] Raj: thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript: occasional mislabels and transcription errors (e.g., KV cash vs KV cache). Benchmarks approximate and based on synthetic 8k seq mix.
notes: Real-world transcript style with some transcription errors; contains links referenced in chat but not included here. recommends 4-hour steady-state run for caching numbers.
